subject: Re: EU processing scope — DPIA inputs, SIG/CAIQ evidence, and VPC peering
messages:
From: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@acme-med.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: gdpr-legal@acme-med.com
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: EU processing scope — DPIA inputs, SIG/CAIQ evidence, and VPC peering

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward an internal security review, our GDPR/privacy team has a few specific asks before we can sign off on a pilot:

- Formal attestation that customer data (PII and derived artifacts) for this account will be processed only within EU regions (no cross-border processing to US or APAC for primary and cold storage).
- A short DPIA input pack we can plug into our internal DPIA (data flows, subprocessors, risk mitigations, retention defaults).
- SIG/CAIQ slices or a callout table mapping your control set to our higher-risk controls (data residency, KMS, key residency, access review cadence).
- Clarification on VPC peering/Private Connect: can we peer to a customer VPC in eu-west-1, and what is the failover behavior if you need to burst to other regions under heavy load? We need the operational boundaries documented.

Can you share the named documents (attestations, SOC2 extracts, sample DPIA inputs) and an ops runbook excerpt for the VPC peering + failover scenario?

Regards,
Sophie Lambert
Head of Privacy Operations
Acme Medical Systems

-----

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@acme-med.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 08:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: EU processing scope — DPIA inputs, SIG/CAIQ evidence, and VPC peering

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vanessa (legal/BD) and Markus (infrastructure) to ensure we cover contractual language and the ops details.

Quick answers up-front:
- Commitment: Redwood can commit to processing customer-submitted content and derived artifacts in EU regions only, subject to the DPA and agreed subprocessors. We document this in an attestation (attached).
- DPIA inputs: we have a short pack with dataflow diagrams, retention/defaults, subprocessors, and risk mitigations — attaching a starter that you can drop into your DPIA.
- SIG/CAIQ: we will provide an extract focused on the controls you called out (data residency, key management, access control reviews).
- VPC peering and failover: short answer — yes, we support VPC peering in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. For capacity events, we do have a configurable burst policy that can route overflow to other regions; that behavior can be disabled for EU-only commitments and we can lock the account to EU-only routing in the control plane. Markus will provide the operational runbook excerpt and options.

We have two attachment stubs I prepared: Redwood EU processing attestation (formal statement) and a SIG/SOC2 extract summary. Markus — can you add the runbook excerpt and the technical note on how we implement a geo-locked peering profile?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

-----

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@acme-med.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: EU processing scope — DPIA inputs, SIG/CAIQ evidence, and VPC peering

Hi Sophie — Markus here (Infra). A few technical clarifications for your ops/security team:

- VPC peering: We offer Private Connect (customer-managed peering) into our EU clusters. Peering endpoints live in the region you select (eu-west-1 or eu-central-1). Network egress for processing stays in-region when "EU-only mode" is enabled.

- Burst/failover: By default, Redwood has three routing tiers: primary-region, same-continent fallback, and global fallback. For EU-only customers we can disable the same-continent fallback and the global fallback, preventing any routing to non-EU capacity. That setting is account-level and requires a signed DPA addendum.

- KMS/Key residency: We support customer-managed keys via KMS in the EU region; keys and key material remain in the region and can be locked to the account. If you require HSM-backed residency (FIPS/HSM), we can discuss the enterprise offering and attestations.

- Audit logs & evidence: We can provide a curated subset of audit logs and a runbook excerpt describing incident escalation and cross-region behavior. Note: raw audit log exports are subject to strict access controls and typically delivered under NDA/SSAE.

I'll attach a short runbook excerpt showing the peering setup, route priorities, and the toggle to lock routing to EU-only.

Regards,
Markus Klein
VP Infra Operations
Redwood Inference

-----

From: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@acme-med.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: gdpr-legal@acme-med.com
Date: Tue, 23 Aug 2027 15:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: EU processing scope — DPIA inputs, SIG/CAIQ evidence, and VPC peering

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple of follow-ups from GDPR team after reviewing your notes:

1) Could you confirm the contractual wording you propose for the DPA addendum that enables the EU-only routing toggle? We prefer a short clause that explicitly prevents transfer unless a specific opt-in is signed.

2) On KMS: can you confirm the supported providers (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) and whether keys can be customer-managed in an HSM-backed configuration? Please flag any additional fees for HSM.

3) For the DPIA pack: can you add a short section on retention defaults (token cache, request logs, embeddings lifetimes) with concrete default TTLs and how they can be configured?

If you can send the DPA clause and updated DPIA pack by EOD Friday, we'll route to legal and privacy for a quick sign-off on the pilot scope.

Best,
Sophie
Head of Privacy Operations
Acme Medical Systems
